newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Tabcorp says Sky Channel ends service to TABs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Tabcorp says Sky Channel ends service to TABs.

text.p: Wagering and gaming group Tabcorp Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday it had failed to negotiate a new supply agreement with Sky Channel and the service to Tabcorp's betting agencies had been cut off.

Sky had rejected a final offer by Tabcorp to pay 2.4 times the original A$3 million annual fee paid for supply of the the sports television channel to its commissioned betting agencies, or TABs, under a contract that ended on June 30, Tabcorp said in a statement. Sky had demanded 2.64 times the original fee.

"Despite Sky's rejection of Tabcorp's offer the company hopes that Sky will reconsider their position and open discussions with Tabcorp in order to restore the service as soon as possible," Tabcorp managing director Ross Wilson said.
Under the old regime, Tabcorp, which operates in the state of Victoria only, passed on about half of the cost of the channnel to its 290 TABs.

Sky, owned equally by businessman Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd and Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd, holds a virtual monopoly on direct tv broadcasts of greyhound, thoroughbred and harness racing in Australia.
The Victorian TABs association has said Sky was vital to attracting punters and more than half of the agencies in the state would have to close if they lost the broadcasts.
The channel has maintained the price increase is intended to recoup the cost of securing sole broadcasting rights for Victorian content.
Tabcorp's Wilson said the loss of Sky could cost the Victorian racing industry up to A$14 million per year in revenue and see a reduction of state government taxation of up to A$18 million per year.
"Tabcorp will take all necessary measures to minimise the impact on the company to ensure that it maintains the profitability of its wagering division in the future," Wilson said.
At 0036 GMT (10.36 a.m.) Tabcorp shares were up one cent to A$5.91.
